findings.issue_text: [BUG] totalPages returns Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, which is one page too many whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, so the pager offers a phantom empty page. An admin paging a group with exactly 50 (or 100, 150...) members at limit 50 sees '2/2' with 'next' still enabled on the real last page; clicking it sets offset to user_count, the server returns zero members, and the page displays an empty '2/2' member list (the same clamping also strands the admin on an empty page after removing the last member of a page).

[BUG] The create action never assigns params[:alias_level] even though the client's asJSON payload sends alias_level with the POST, so every new group is persisted with the column default of 0. An admin who selects a non-default alias level on the new-group form and saves gets a server-side group with alias_level 0 ('nobody can alias') while the client model still shows the chosen value, so the group silently runs with wrong aliasing permissions until someone happens to re-save it via update.

[BUG] The members action now hard-caps every group at 50 rows (limit defaults to 50) while the public group members template gained no pagination controls, replacing the old behavior that returned all members (up to 200 for automatic groups). Any visitor to /groups/:name/members of a group with more than 50 members sees only the first 50 with no indication or any way to reach the rest — large public groups' member lists are silently truncated.

[BUG] add_members calls group.add(user) for every supplied username with no check that the user is already a member, and the admin UI's addMembers action deliberately leaves the usernames input populated after a successful add (the in-code TODO), so clicking Add twice re-submits the same usernames. Re-adding an existing member inserts a second group_users row (member listed twice, user_count inflated) or raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique for a 500, and the admin receives no feedback in either case; no spec in the diff covers duplicate adds.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips any username for which User.find_by_username returns nil (including space-padded entries like 'bob, alice') and still renders success_json. An admin who typos a username or pastes a comma-space-separated list is told the operation succeeded while those members were never added; the old spec that documented this silent-skip behavior was deleted along with the PATCH endpoint, so nothing in the suite pins or surfaces it.

[ADVISORY] The /groups/:name/members response changes from a bare serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} with no versioning or transitional support in either direction. During a rolling deploy or for any browser holding a cached pre-deploy JS bundle, old clients run result.map on the new object and new clients run result.meta.total on the old array — both throw TypeError, leaving the public members page and the admin group page with an empty member list until the client reloads.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten update action reads only name/alias_level/visible, so the previously accepted membership payloads — PUT with group[usernames] and PATCH with changes[add]/changes[delete] — are now silently ignored instead of rejected. Any existing script or integration that manages Discourse group membership via PUT/PATCH /admin/groups/:id receives a 200 success while membership is unchanged — a silent no-op with no error signaling that the contract moved to the new /admin/groups/:id/members endpoints.

[BUG] The public group members route now calls model.findMembers(), which fetches only the first 50 members (Group#limit defaults to 50), while the diff adds pagination controls only to the admin template, so the public members page silently drops every member past the first 50. A user opening /groups/:name/members for a group with 200 members sees 50 rows and no pager — the old code rendered all members (200 for automatic groups) — so the majority of a large group's membership becomes unreachable on the public page with no error or indication.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which overstates the page count by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and the next action (lines 29-38) clamps offset to user_count, so the pager navigates the admin onto an empty page. For a group with exactly 100 members and limit 50, totalPages is 3, so from page 2 the admin can click next to offset 100; the server returns zero members and the admin sees an empty '3/3' member list.

[BUG] removeMember reloads the list via findMembers without adjusting offset, and findMembers clamps offset against the stale pre-fetch user_count (line 23), so removing the last member of the last page reloads to an empty page. With 51 members (limit 50) the admin on page 2 removes the single listed member; the reload requests offset 50 against the new total of 50, gets zero members back, and the admin is stranded on an empty '2/2' page until clicking previous.

[BUG] update reads flat params (params[:visible], params[:alias_level], params[:name]) and drops the nested group[...] contract the removed update_put required, so a PUT from any existing API client in the old format silently forces visible to false and no-ops the requested changes. A client still sending PUT /admin/groups/:id with group: {visible: 'true', alias_level: 3} (or the removed PATCH changes payload) receives success_json while the group's visible flag is flipped to false and no alias or membership change is applied — silent data corruption behind a success response.

[BUG] create never assigns alias_level even though the admin form shows the alias-level combo box for new groups and the client's asJSON sends alias_level, so every newly created group is stored with alias_level 0. An admin who selects 'members, mods and admins' while creating a group gets a group where nobody can use the alias; the UI keeps showing the chosen value client-side, so the drop is invisible until a reload.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten public members action — new default limit 50, offset applied to every group, and a new {members, meta} envelope replacing the bare serialized array — ships with no spec anywhere in the diff (the only test file touched is the admin controller spec). The meta contract (total/limit/offset) that both the public members page and the admin pager parse is untested; a regression in the envelope or the pagination SQL ships green and breaks both pages plus every consumer of /groups/:name/members.

[ADVISORY] The diff rewrites Admin::GroupsController#update to a new flat-parameter contract and deletes the old 'is able to update group members' spec, leaving the new .update context with only the automatic-group name test — no test updates a normal group. Nothing verifies that PUT /admin/groups/:id persists name, alias_level, or visible for a non-automatic group under the new contract, so a mismatch between the keys asJSON sends and the keys update reads passes the entire suite and reaches production as silent update failures.

[ADVISORY] The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec drives remove_member with xhr :put even though config/routes.rb maps only DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member, and controller specs bypass routing entirely. The automatic-group guard is verified through a request no real client can make; if the DELETE route is dropped or remapped, this acceptance test stays green while the actual endpoint 404s for every caller including the shipped UI.

[ADVISORY] addMembers never clears the usernames input after a successful add — the author's own '// TODO: should clear the input' marks the missing step — so the just-added names stay in the selector. The admin's next click on Add re-submits the same usernames against add_members, which silently skips existing members and returns success, leaving the admin with no signal that nothing happened.

[ADVISORY] remove_member removes membership with group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing the existing Group#remove method that the deleted PATCH path used, leaving two divergent removal mechanisms in the codebase. Any behavior Group#remove performs beyond the raw join delete (destroy callbacks, cache invalidation) is silently skipped on the admin path, and the next change to removal semantics must be duplicated in both places or the admin UI drifts from every other caller of Group#remove.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the specs that pinned add/remove edge cases ('succeeds silently when adding non-existent users', 'succeeds silently when removing non-members') and the replacement .add_members/.remove_member contexts contain no equivalent tests, so the retained `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` silent-skip guards are unverified. If someone tightens the guard to raise on unknown usernames or swaps it for find_by_username!, no test fails; meanwhile an admin who typos a username gets a success response while nothing was added, with no error surfaced anywhere in the new UI.

[BUG] The public group members route now loads members through the paginated findMembers() (model default limit 50) while the public members template gained no pagination controls, so the page that previously listed every member now silently truncates. End users opening the Members tab of a group with more than 50 members can no longer see members 51+ at all — the old endpoint returned the full list (200 for automatic groups) and this page has no next/previous control to reach them.

[BUG] The rewritten create action persists only name and visible, silently discarding the alias_level that the rewritten client asJSON() sends in the POST body. An admin who selects an alias level on the new-group form and clicks Save receives a 200 while the group is stored with alias_level 0; the combo box keeps displaying the chosen value, so the wrong persisted state stays invisible until the page is reloaded.

[BUG] update reads only top-level params (name/alias_level/visible) while the previous release's client PUT the old {group: {...}} payload and PATCH /admin/groups/:id (still routed here by resources :groups) previously handled changes: {add/delete} — neither old payload shape is rejected. An admin tab still running the pre-deploy client that saves a group gets a success response while the new server assigns visible = false (params[:visible] is nil so the == "true" comparison yields false) and silently drops the name/alias_level/usernames edits; out-of-tree PATCH callers sending changes payloads likewise receive a 200 no-op.

[BUG] totalPages returns Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which overcounts by one page whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the page size. For any group with exactly 50 (or 100, 150, ...) members the admin pager shows "1/2" with next enabled; clicking it clamps offset to user_count (50), the server returns an empty member list, and the admin lands on an empty "2/2" page that looks like the group lost its members.

[BUG] findMembers clamps the request offset against the pre-fetch user_count and then writes the server-echoed meta.offset back into the model, so an offset that was valid before a removal is preserved on a page that no longer exists. With 51 members (limit 50), removing the single member shown on page 2 reloads at offset 50 against the now-50-member group, stranding the admin on an empty "2/2" page even though 50 members remain, recoverable only by clicking previous.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten update action's primary path is left untested: the only .update spec covers ignoring name changes on automatic groups, and the deleted "is able to update group members" spec was never replaced. A regression in the new top-level-param update handling — renaming a non-automatic group, assigning alias_level, or the render_json_error path — breaks every admin group edit and ships green because no spec exercises it; the alias_level drop in create is exactly the class of bug this gap lets through.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips usernames that match no user and still renders success_json, and the diff deletes the spec that pinned this behavior ("succeeds silently when adding non-existent users") without replacing it. An admin who typos a username in the new Add members box gets a success response and a reloaded list that simply lacks the user, with no error anywhere; the behavior is also now unpinned, so a future change to raise a 422 (or to break the skip) ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] The public /groups/:name/members response changed from a bare serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} and the default limit dropped from unbounded (200 for automatic groups) to 50, with no compatibility or versioning path. Any plugin, theme, or API consumer that parses the old array response or relied on receiving all members breaks silently when this deploys — in-tree callers were updated in lockstep but out-of-tree consumers receive an object where they expect an array.

[ADVISORY] This group-memberships PR also restyles the badges admin form: the label/input-width rules were deleted from section.details .form-horizontal and re-added only under a new ".groups, .badges" scope, which is work not traceable to the stated intent. Any admin page that relied on the deleted section.details .form-horizontal rules without a .groups or .badges ancestor class (the badges details form, if its markup lacks a .badges wrapper) silently loses its 350px input widths and bold labels, and badges styling now changes in lockstep with unrelated group styling.

[ADVISORY] remove_member deletes the membership with the raw association call group.users.delete(user_id) while its sibling add_members uses the domain method group.add(user), abandoning Group#remove which this diff's own removed code still called. Any side effect Group#remove performs beyond join-row deletion (destroy callbacks, counter or cache updates) is silently skipped on admin removals, and the add/remove paths diverge so a future fix to Group#remove never applies to this endpoint.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten public members action feeds params[:limit] and params[:offset] straight into the SQL limit/offset with no non-negative validation. Any user can request /groups/:name/members?limit=-1 (or a negative offset) and trigger a 500 from PostgreSQL's "LIMIT must not be negative" instead of a 4xx — a hole the rewrite extends from automatic groups to every group.

[ADVISORY] addMembers ships with an in-code TODO ("should clear the input") acknowledging the user-selector is never cleared after a successful add. After adding a batch the stale usernames stay in the input, so the admin must manually clear them before the next batch and a second click of Add re-sends the same names; the field itself never confirms the add happened.

[BUG] The new form adds <label for="name"> but {{text-field name="name"}} renders an input whose id is Ember's generated emberNNN, so the for attribute references an id that no element has. Clicking the Name label does nothing and assistive technology cannot associate the label with its input — the new markup asserts an association the rendered DOM does not provide.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, which overstates the page count by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, so showingLast never fires on the real last page and the next action (line 33) advances offset to user_count, which the server answers with an empty member list. An admin viewing a group with exactly 50/100/150… members clicks next on the last real page and lands on a blank '2/2' (or '3/3') page with zero members rendered; the correct formula is Math.ceil(user_count/limit).

[BUG] The public group members route issues a single model.findMembers() with the model defaults (limit 50, offset 0) and the diff adds no pagination controls to group/members.hbs, so members past the first 50 are unreachable from the public page. Users visiting the public members page of a group with more than 50 members can no longer see the remaining members at all — a regression from the previous behavior of listing every member (up to 200 for automatic groups).

[BUG] The rewritten update/create actions changed the admin groups API contract without versioning: the params[:group][...] envelope and the PATCH changes[add]/[delete] branch were dropped, and group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" now assigns false whenever the param is absent. An existing admin-API client that PUTs group: {name: 'x'} receives success_json while its rename is ignored and the group is silently flipped to invisible; a PATCH membership change now no-ops with a success response; a JSON-body client sending visible: true as a boolean also gets visible=false.

[BUG] The public /groups/:name/members response changed from a bare serialized array (render_serialized(members.to_a, ...)) to an object {members: [...], meta: {...}} with no versioning or compatibility period. Any client running the previous frontend build (cached assets after deploy) or an external consumer of the endpoint executes result.map on the new object and throws, leaving the group members view blank until assets refresh.

[BUG] removeMember reloads via self.findMembers() with the offset unchanged, so when a removal empties the current page the server returns an empty list for a now-past-the-end offset and nothing adjusts the page back. With 51 members, page 2 shows one member; removing that member leaves the admin staring at an empty '2/2' page that looks like the member list was wiped until they click previous.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips every username that fails to resolve — a typo, a space after the comma ('bob, alice' yields ' alice'), or a group name picked from the user-selector autocomplete — and still renders success_json. An admin who adds a mistyped username gets a success response and a reloaded list without the member, with no error identifying which username failed, and the input still holds the dead text (the clear-input TODO is unimplemented), inviting blind retries.

[ADVISORY] The members action applies no server-side clamping to the client-supplied limit and offset before passing them to limit()/offset() on a public endpoint. A request with a negative offset reaches SQL and raises a 500, and an uncapped limit lets a single request materialize and serialize a large group's entire membership, reintroducing the unbounded-response load the pagination was meant to remove.

[ADVISORY] create reads only params[:name] and params[:visible] and never assigns alias_level, while the rewritten admin form presents the alias-level combo box for unsaved groups and the client sends alias_level in the POST body. An admin who sets the alias level while creating a group silently gets alias_level 0 and must notice the loss and re-save after creation.

[BUG] The rewritten members action caps every group listing at 50 (the new default limit) while this diff adds pagination controls only to the admin group page, so the public /groups/:name/members page — whose route and template this same diff retargets onto the paginated findMembers — silently truncates to the first 50 members. Any user opening the public members page of a group with more than 50 members can no longer see or reach members 51+: before this diff non-automatic groups returned the full member list (automatic groups up to 200), and the new page shows no pager and no indication that members are hidden.

[BUG] The rewritten update action unconditionally executes group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" and reads only the new flat params, so a PUT or PATCH carrying the previous payload format (group: {...} or changes: {...}) sets visible to false, applies no other change, and returns success. An admin whose tab still runs the pre-deploy JavaScript — or any external admin-API client using the old group[usernames]/changes format — 'saves' a group and silently flips it to hidden (visible=false) while the submitted name, alias_level and membership changes are discarded, all behind a 200 success response.

[ADVISORY] The public endpoint GET /groups/:name/members changes its response contract from a bare serialized array to a {members, meta} envelope with no compatibility period, versioning, or feature flag. Every consumer still parsing the old array breaks: browsers running the pre-deploy JavaScript call result.map() on the new object and throw a TypeError that leaves the group members UI blank until a hard reload (new JS against an old backend crashes on result.meta.total the same way), and any plugin or external script fetching member lists receives an object where it expects an array.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which overstates the page count by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (it must be Math.ceil). A group with exactly 50 (or 100, 150, ...) members renders the admin pager as '1/2' with the next arrow enabled, and clicking it navigates to an empty member page showing '2/2' — the admin hits a phantom page on every exact-multiple group.

[BUG] The rewritten create action reads only params[:name] and params[:visible] while the frontend posts asJSON() verbatim — which includes alias_level — so the alias level selected in the new-group form is silently discarded and the group is created with alias_level 0. An admin who creates a group with alias level 'members, mods and admins' gets a group where nobody can mention or message it (alias_level 0); the form keeps displaying the chosen value while the server stored 0, so the divergence is invisible until a page reload.

[BUG] removeMember's success callback reloads via findMembers(), which clamps offset against the stale pre-removal user_count and then adopts the server-echoed offset, so nothing pulls the pager back when the member count shrinks across a page boundary. With 101 members and the admin on page 3, removing that page's single member reloads offset=100 against the 100 remaining members and renders an empty member list labeled '3/3' — the admin must notice and click previous before any member is visible.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips any username that matches no user and still returns success_json, and this diff deletes the spec ('succeeds silently when adding non-existent users') that pinned exactly that behavior. An admin who typos a username in the free-text 'enter username' field gets a success response and a member-list reload that simply lacks the user, with no error anywhere — and no test remains to catch a future change to this silent-skip behavior.

[ADVISORY] Nothing ever resets the controller's usernames value — not after a successful add (the code carries a 'TODO: should clear the input') and not in setupController when switching groups — even though the admin-group controller is a singleton reused across every group. Usernames typed while viewing group A are still sitting in the input when the admin opens group B, so clicking Add on B submits A's leftover usernames to B's add_members endpoint and silently adds the wrong users to the wrong group; clicking Add twice on the same group also re-submits the same names.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the only spec that exercised a normal (non-automatic) group update — rename plus settings — and replaces it with a single spec covering only the automatic-group path, leaving the rewritten update's live branches (the alias_level assignment and the non-automatic rename on line 40) untested. A future regression in group renaming or alias-level saving breaks every admin group edit while CI stays green, because no test in the suite executes those branches.

[BUG] Admin::GroupsController#remove_member looks up the group with `Group.find(params[:id].to_i)` — the line carried over unchanged from the old `destroy` action — but the new member route `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` inside `resources :groups` binds the group id as `params[:group_id]`, and both the client (`Discourse.Group#removeMember` requesting `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json`) and the diff's own specs supply `group_id`, never `id`. In every real request `params[:id]` is nil, so `Group.find(0)` raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound and the endpoint returns 404 — the admin UI's remove-member button never removes anyone — and both new specs (`xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: group.id, ...` expecting success, and `group_id: 1` expecting 422) fail against this code.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten public `GroupsController#members` feeds the user-supplied `limit` straight into `group.users.limit(limit)` with no server-side upper bound (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`). Any visitor who can see a group sends `?limit=100000000` and receives the group's entire membership serialized in one response — for the visible automatic `everyone` group that is the site's full user list — so the pagination this diff adds is trivially bypassed and each such request is a cheap heavy DB/serialization load for the site operator.

[ADVISORY] `update` silently changes the payload contract of the existing `PUT /admin/groups/:id` endpoint: it now reads top-level `params[:alias_level]/[:visible]/[:name]` instead of the previous `params[:group][...]` envelope, drops the `usernames` membership field entirely, and still replies with `success_json`. Any existing admin-API consumer still PUTting the old `group[...]` payload gets a 200 while its changes are silently discarded — `params[:visible]` being nil even forces `visible` to false — so a membership-revocation/offboarding call reports success while the removed user stays in the group retaining access to its gated content.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten `.update` context contains only the automatic-group test, so no test in this diff exercises the non-automatic success path of the rewritten update action — `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i` (controller lines 38), `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` (line 39) and `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` (line 41) — even though the diff changed the wire format from params[:group][:name] to flat params[:name] and deleted the old test that verified rename (`group.name.should == 'fred'`). A regression in the new flat-param reading (e.g., reverting to params[:group][:name] or a typo'd alias_level key) makes every admin rename/alias-level edit a silent no-op — the server returns success_json, nothing persists — and the suite stays green because the only .update test hits group 1 (automatic), where the name assignment is skipped by design; I checked the only test file in the diff (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb) and its final .update context has exactly one test.

[ADVISORY] The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" test invokes the action with `xhr :put, :remove_member` although this diff routes remove_member as DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, routes.rb line 49) and the sibling happy-path test correctly uses `xhr :delete` (line 125) — the verb is a copy-paste from the .add_members context. The spec misdocuments the endpoint: a developer wiring a client from this test sends PUT /admin/groups/:id/members, which routes to add_members in production and fails on params.require(:usernames) instead of returning the documented 422; functional specs bypass routing, so the suite also never pins the DELETE verb — flipping the route verb keeps every test green.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users" from the old incremental update tests while porting the same behavior into add_members (`if user = User.find_by_username(username)`), and no test in the new .add_members context executes that skip branch — the automatic-group test returns at the guard before the loop runs and the happy test uses two valid usernames. The intended semantics for unknown usernames (silently skipped, 200 success) are now unpinned: a change to raise on unknown users (turning an admin's typo into a 500) or to drop the guard entirely passes the suite, and admins adding a misspelled username get a success response with the member silently absent; checked spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb (the only test file in the diff), whose .add_members context (lines 91-110) contains only the guard and happy-path tests.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes "succeeds silently when removing non-members" and no replacement test removes a user who is not a member, so remove_member's no-op path (`group.users.delete(user_id)` for a non-member followed by success_json) is unverified — the only remove_member tests are the automatic guard (422) and the happy path. Any change to how non-member removal behaves (raising, 404, or an accidental no-op success) ships green; the realistic trigger is an admin clicking remove on a stale member list after another admin already removed the user, and the suite cannot detect the behavior change; checked spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb, whose .remove_member context (lines 112-132) covers only those two paths.

[ADVISORY] Both new membership specs hand-feed `group_id`/`user_id` straight to the actions (`xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, ...` here, and again at lines 103, 115, 125), so no test in the diff exercises the new member routes or pins the Rails bare-member-route convention that supplies `params[:group_id]` — a different param name than the `params[:id]` the same controller's update/destroy rely on. A routing refactor that changes the supplied param name (e.g., moving the routes into a `member do` block, which yields params[:id]) leaves the entire suite green while every production add/remove membership call raises ActionController::ParameterMissing; the specs mirror the controller's param names instead of verifying them, and the diff contains no request-level spec for these endpoints.

[ADVISORY] The sole `.create` test posts only `name: " bob "` and asserts nothing about `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` (controller line 26) — the test itself creates the group with visible=false (nil == "true") without noticing, and no test passes `visible` to create even though the real client (group.js asJSON) always sends it. A regression in create's visible reading (e.g., `params[:visible].present?`, which maps an unchecked box to true, or a wire-format change from the frontend's boolean) silently creates groups with the wrong visibility — a privacy-affecting setting — and the suite stays green; checked spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb, whose .create context (lines 34-47) contains only the name-stripping test.

[BUG] update reads only the new flat params (params[:visible], params[:name], params[:alias_level]) and drops all handling of the review-base nested group[...] payload (including group[usernames] and the PATCH changes[add/delete] form), so an old-payload PUT finds params[:visible] nil and line 38 unconditionally assigns group.visible = false while discarding every other requested change, then returns success_json. Any caller still on the old contract — an admin whose browser holds the pre-deploy JS bundle in an open tab, or any external script/plugin using the existing admin groups API — silently has the group's visible flag flipped to false (hiding the group from non-members) and its membership edits silently discarded, all with a 200 success response; the payload contract changed in one step with no expand/contract compatibility layer.

[BUG] The members endpoint's response schema is replaced in a single step — from the bare serialized array that review-base clients consume to a {members, meta} envelope — with no transition period, versioned endpoint, or shape negotiation. The review-base frontend's findMembers does result.map(...) on the response and throws TypeError against the new envelope, while the new frontend's result.meta.total throws against the old array, so during any rolling deploy or asset-cache skew the group members page crashes for whichever side is stale, and out-of-tree API consumers parsing the array format break permanently.

[BUG] The public group members page issues a single model.findMembers() (default limit 50) in setupController, and this diff adds no pagination controls to the public members template, so the membership list is silently truncated at 50 rows. Users viewing any group with more than 50 members see only the first 50 with no indication and no way to page — a regression from review-base, which returned all members for non-automatic groups (and up to 200 for automatic ones) — e.g., a 300-member public group appears to have 50 members.

[BUG] totalPages returns Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which overstates the page count by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, so showingLast is false on the last populated page and the next control navigates to an empty page (the next action's clamp Math.min(offset + limit, user_count) lands offset exactly on user_count, where the API returns zero rows). An admin paging a group with exactly 50 (or 100, 150, ...) members clicks next from the last populated page and lands on an empty member list rendered as '2/2' or '3/3', making it look like the group's members disappeared.

[ADVISORY] create accepts only the new flat params[:name]/params[:visible] shape and rejects the review-base nested group[...] payload, changing the admin API's create contract in one step with no compatibility path for old callers. A stale admin client (pre-deploy JS cached in an open tab) or an external script POSTing the old group: {name: ..., usernames: ...} payload gets name = '' and a 422 validation error, so group creation fails for those callers during the deploy window — loudly, unlike the update path, but with no deprecation or dual-shape acceptance to bridge the transition.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which overcounts by one page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and the next action (line 33) then advances offset to user_count, landing the admin on that empty page. For a group with exactly 50 members the admin clicks next from page 1/2, the client requests offset=50, the server returns zero members, and the page displays an empty member list labeled '2/2' — the admin sees the membership apparently cut in half with no explanation.

[BUG] next commits group.set("offset", offset) before the findMembers() request resolves — and previous does the same at line 46 — with no rollback and no rejection handler, so a failed request leaves the committed offset in place. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] removeMember and addMembers have no rejection handling anywhere in the chain — the model methods attach no .catch, the inner self.findMembers() reload is neither returned nor caught, and the controller actions discard the returned promises — so a failed membership mutation is invisible. When the PUT/DELETE to /admin/groups/<id>/members.json fails (500, dropped connection), the admin who clicked Add or the remove × sees nothing: no error, no state change, no pending indicator; and even after a successful mutation a failed reload leaves the stale member list with no signal, so the admin cannot tell whether the membership changed.

adjudication.rationale: In `discourse/models/group.js`, both `addMembers` and `removeMember` do `return Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` but they neither return the `findMembers()` promise nor attach any rejection handling. That means a failure in the reload request (`findMembers` -> `Discourse.ajax('/groups/<name>/members.json', ...)`) cannot be observed/handled by the original add/remove promise chain. Additionally, in `admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6`, `addMembers` does not return the model promise at all (`this.get("model").addMembers(...)`), and `removeMember` triggers `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` inside the bootbox callback without returning/catching it, so the action layer also provides no way to surface failures. The diff shows no other UI error/pending-state handling around these calls, making silent failures and stale member lists a real risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] setupController fires model.findMembers() without returning the promise or attaching any rejection handler, so a failed fetch leaves the public group members page silently empty. A user viewing /g/<name>/members when the members request fails (403 after the group was made invisible, 500, network drop) gets an empty member table with no error; the removed afterModel propagated the rejection and aborted the transition, so the failure was visible before this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`, the route no longer returns the `model.findMembers()` promise from `afterModel` (the `afterModel` hook was removed entirely) and instead calls `model.findMembers();` in `setupController` without `return` or error handling. `Discourse.Group#findMembers` performs `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` and returns that promise, so if the request rejects (403/500/network), nothing in the route will block/abort the transition or surface the error; the template was also changed to render `{{#each m in members}}`, which depends on the `members` property set only on success. This makes it plausible the members list renders empty/undefined on failure where previously a rejected `afterModel` promise would have been propagated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The public members page now fetches through findMembers(), which sends the model's default limit of 50, and the diff adds no pagination controls to group/members.hbs, so the page silently truncates the membership at 50. Every group with more than 50 members shows only the first 50 on its public members page, with no indicator and no way to view the rest — a regression from the previous server behavior that returned all members (200 for automatic groups); users and staff conclude members are missing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit`/`offset` with a default limit of 50 (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`, `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`), and `Discourse.Group#findMembers()` now calls `/groups/:name/members.json` passing the model’s `limit` (default `50`) and `offset`. The public route `group-members.js.es6` now just calls `model.findMembers()` and the public template `group/members.hbs` iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no pagination UI or controls added there. Therefore, for groups with >50 members, only the first page of 50 will be shown with no indication or way to navigate, which is a behavior regression from the prior endpoint that returned all members (or 200 for automatic groups).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] create ignores params[:alias_level] even though the client's asJSON() sends alias_level on the POST, so the alias level selected in the new-group form is silently dropped at creation. An admin who creates a group with alias level 'mods and admins' gets a group persisted with alias_level 0 ('nobody') while the still-open form shows their selection; the choice is lost with a 200 success and only surfaces as wrong group permissions after a reload.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#create`, the server only sets `group.name` and `group.visible` (from `params[:name]` / `params[:visible]`) and never assigns `alias_level` from params. Meanwhile the client `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` includes `alias_level` and `create()` POSTs it as top-level data (`Discourse.ajax("/admin/groups", { type: "POST", data: this.asJSON() })`). Therefore, when creating a new group, any selected alias level is silently ignored and the persisted group will use the model/default alias_level (likely 0), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] update keeps the same PUT /admin/groups/:id route but reads only the new flat params (params[:name], params[:alias_level], params[:visible]) and ignores the old {group: {...}} payload shape, returning success_json for requests whose entire payload was dropped. During the deploy window any admin tab still running the old JS sends {group: {name, alias_level, visible, usernames}} via saveWithUsernames; the new handler reads no top-level visible param and sets group.visible = false, drops the membership changes entirely, and returns 200 — the group silently becomes invisible and the admin's membership edits silently no-op while the UI reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the code now reads only flat params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) and no longer looks at the previous nested payload (`params[:group]`), which the old `update_put` implementation used. Because it unconditionally does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`, a request that sends only `{ group: { visible: "true", ... } }` (with no top-level `visible`) will set `visible` to `false` (nil == "true"). It also drops membership/usernames updates entirely. The route remains the same (`PUT /admin/groups/:id`), so mixed old/new JS during deploy could cause silent incorrect updates while still returning `success_json` (200).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] add_members silently skips every username that does not resolve to a user (User.find_by_username returns nil) and then renders success_json, reporting success for the dropped work. An admin who submits a misspelled username — or a pasted list like 'bob, alice' where the space after the comma breaks find_by_username — receives a 200 and a reloaded member list without the member: no error, no log, no indication which name failed, so the add appears accepted and simply does nothing.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, usernames are processed via `usernames.split(",").each` and each token is passed directly to `User.find_by_username(username)`; if it returns nil the name is silently ignored, and the action still renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it likely will even if nothing was added). There’s no stripping/normalization of whitespace, no error reporting, and no indication of which usernames failed. This is a concrete, diff-grounded validation/UX gap, but the diff doesn’t establish that the endpoint is required to fail on unknown usernames, so it’s not conclusively a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] offset = params[:offset].to_i is passed to .offset() with no lower clamp, so a client-supplied negative offset reaches PostgreSQL as OFFSET -n. GET /groups/<name>/members.json?offset=-1 raises 'OFFSET must not be negative' (ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid) and returns an HTML 500 on this public endpoint instead of a 4xx; the Ember client clamps its own offset, but any API consumer sending a negative value gets a 500.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then calls `group.users...offset(offset)` with no validation/clamp (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb). A client can supply `offset=-1`, which will be passed through to ActiveRecord/PostgreSQL as a negative OFFSET and can raise an error (server 500) on this public endpoint. The Ember client clamping doesn’t protect other API consumers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no maximum, so a single request can demand the group's entire membership in one response. Any signed-in user who can see a large group (trust-level automatic groups can have hundreds of thousands of members) sends ?limit=99999999 and forces the server to load and serialize every member row at once — trivially repeatable DB and serialization load on a public endpoint; a one-line cap closes it.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound. This is a public-ish endpoint (guarded only by `guardian.ensure_can_see!`) and the response serializes `members`, so an attacker can request an extremely large `?limit=` value to force large DB reads and serialization work. The finding’s suggested cap is directly applicable to the new code.
